title: The Cosmic Web: Filaments, Walls and the Warm-Hot Intergalactic Medium Baryon Budget Against Density Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Wulan Rahmawati, and this is The Cosmic Web: Filaments, Walls and the Warm-Hot Intergalactic Medium Baryon Budget Against Density Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Wulan Rahmawati, and this is The Cosmic Web: Filaments, Walls and the Warm-Hot Intergalactic Medium Baryon Budget Against Density Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Accretion Shock Temperatures of Filament Gas: The Inflow Speeds That Manufacture the Warm-Hot Phase'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): v_km_s = 100, T_postshock_K = 134000.0, Mach = 7.1, line_density_for_vesc_Msun_per_Mpc = 581000000000.0; v_km_s = 200, T_postshock_K = 536000.0, Mach = 14.0, line_density_for_vesc_Msun_per_Mpc = 2330000000000.0; v_km_s = 300, T_postshock_K = 1210000.0, Mach = 21.0, line_density_for_vesc_Msun_per_Mpc = 5230000000000.0; v_km_s = 400, T_postshock_K = 2140000.0, Mach =
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Baryon Conversion Efficiency by Cosmic-Web Environment: Where Stars Formed from the Available Gas'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): global_stellar_share_of_baryons = 0.07; stellar_fraction_of_baryons_in_voids = 0.03231; stellar_fraction_of_baryons_in_walls = 0.06417; stellar_fraction_of_baryons_in_filaments = 0.08; stellar_fraction_of_baryons_in_nodes = 0.08; efficiency_nodes_over_voids = 2.48; efficiency_filaments_over_global = 1.14; unconverted_baryon_share_in_filaments = 0.92.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Broad Lyman-Alpha Absorbers: Temperature Ceilings from Line Widths and the Baryon Share of the Broad-Line Population'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): b_km_s = 50.0; T_ceiling_from_b_K = 151000.0; N_HI_cm2 = 30000000000000.0; adopted_f_HI = 1e-05; inferred_NH_cm2 = 3e+18; dNdz = 30.0; BLA_fraction_of_baryons = 0.028; fraction_if_fHI_3e-6 = 0.0933; fraction_if_fHI_3e-5 = 0.00933; b_thermal_at_1e5K_km_s = 41.0; b_thermal_at_3e5K_km_s = 70.0.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Cooling Times and Entropy of Warm-Hot Filament Gas: Why the Phase, Once Heated, Persists'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): ne_cm3 = 1e-05, T_K = 1000000.0, t_cool_Gyr = 18.1, tcool_over_tHubble = 1.25, entropy_K_keV_cm2 = 186.0; ne_cm3 = 1e-05, T_K = 10000000.0, t_cool_Gyr = 904.0, tcool_over_tHubble = 62.3, entropy_K_keV_cm2 = 1860.0; ne_cm3 = 0.0001, T_K = 1000000.0, t_cool_Gyr = 1.81, tcool_over_tHubble = 0.125, entropy_K_keV_cm2 = 40.0; ne_cm3 = 0.0001, T_K = 10000000.0, t_cool_Gyr
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Cosmic Walls: Surface Density, Face-On Columns and Collapse Timescales of the Sheet Component'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): wall_overdensity = 5.0; thickness_Mpc = 3.0; baryon_surface_density_Msun_pc2 = 0.0932; NH_face_on_cm2 = 8.85e+18; DM_face_on_pc_cm3 = 3.32; free_fall_time_Gyr = 18.2; Hubble_time_Gyr = 14.5; wall_volume_share_input = 0.16; wall_mass_share_two_phase_estimate = 0.488; electron_column_cm2 = 1.02e+19.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Dispersion and Faraday Rotation per Filament Crossing: The Per-Structure Budgets Behind the Line-of-Sight Totals'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): ne_cm3 = 6.6e-06; path_Mpc = 2.5; B_parallel_nG = 20.0; DM_per_crossing_pc_cm3 = 16.5; RM_per_crossing_rad_m2 = 0.267; band_delay_400_800MHz_ms = 321.0; crossings_to_z1 = 22.0; total_filament_DM_to_z1 = 363.0; RM_rms_random_walk_rad_m2 = 1.25; DM_per_crossing_if_overdensity_10 = 5.5; DM_per_crossing_if_overdensity_100 = 55.0.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Accretion Shock Temperatures of Filament Gas: The Inflow Speeds That Manufacture the Warm-Hot Phase”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): v_km_s = 100, T_postshock_K = 134000.0, Mach = 7.1, line_density_for_vesc_Msun_per_Mpc = 581000000000.0; v_km_s = 200, T_postshock_K = 536000.0, Mach = 14.0, line_density_for_vesc_Msun_per_Mpc = 2330000000000.0; v_km_s = 300, T_postshock_K = 12100 (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Accretion Shock Temperatures of Filament Gas: The Inflow Speeds That Manufacture the Warm-Hot Phase'; 'Baryon Conversion Efficiency by Cosmic-Web Environment: Where Stars Formed from the Available Gas'; 'Broad Lyman-Alpha Absorbers: Temperature Ceilings from Line Widths and the Baryon Share of the Broad-Line Population'; 'Cooling Times and Entropy of Warm-Hot Filament Gas: Why the Phase, Once Heated, Persists'; 'Cosmic Walls: Surface Density, Face-On Columns and Collapse Timescales of the Sheet Component'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
